subject.title: fix(codex): scoped tool allowlist blocks the user MCP servers it explicitly allows

question: Should scoped static user MCP servers permanently use OpenClaw dynamic-tool naming and approval semantics instead of Codex-native MCP attachment, or is an app-server-native scoped attachment contract required?
rationale: The patch intentionally changes the ownership boundary for an access-controlled external-tool surface; source-level tests alone cannot decide the durable user-facing and security contract.

options.title: Accept dynamic scoped tools
options.body: Treat the dynamic-tool bridge as the supported scoped-MCP contract after live proof verifies exact allowlist enforcement and no native duplicate attachment.

options.title: Require native scoped attachment
options.body: Pause this implementation and define a Codex-supported native per-tool MCP contract if preserving Codex-native tool identity and approvals is required.

recommendation.title: Accept dynamic scoped tools
recommendation.body: Treat the dynamic-tool bridge as the supported scoped-MCP contract after live proof verifies exact allowlist enforcement and no native duplicate attachment.

likelyOwner.reason: Their prior adjacent implementation and stated focus on this exact attachment-policy boundary make them the best evidence-backed routing candidate available in the supplied context.
